statement.essentials: Taking out part of the gland can leave a visible hollow in the cheek. The space is sometimes filled, but in most operations it is not.
statement.anatomy: A reduction in the volume of the cheek after the gland is removed is called a contour deformity. Reconstruction of the volume or contour is done to address it.
statement.clinical: A systematic review of 235 studies pooled a deformity rate of 11.8% (95% CI 6.9 to 19.5), with aesthetic problems worse after more extensive resections. In a US database of 11,057 parotidectomies, volume or contour reconstruction was relatively uncommon, at 18%.

numbers.label: Deformity after parotidectomy
numbers.population: Patients in studies of parotidectomy reporting minor complications

numbers.label: Volume or contour reconstruction at parotidectomy
numbers.population: Patients in the US ACS-NSQIP database having parotidectomy, 2012 to 2017
numbers.design: Retrospective database review identified by procedure codes

limitations: How deformity was defined and graded differed between the pooled studies, and the database counts only what was coded, so the 18% may under-report. The hollow in the model is drawn at an illustrative depth, not a measured one.
